extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, reexamination clerks, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards from the MPEP for handling ex parte reexamination papers, responses, amendments, petitions, service, defective papers, final actions, and revival petitions in U.S. reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling bona fide incomplete responses after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a bona fide response to an examiner’s action is filed after final rejection (but within the permissible response period) and some point necessary to fully respond has been omitted through apparent oversight or inadvertence, the examiner should not issue a notice of failure to fully respond; rather, an advisory Office action (form PTOL-467) should be issued with an explanation of the omission. The time period set in the final rejection continues to run and is extended by 1 month if the response is the first response after the final rejection in accordance with MPEP § 2265. See also MPEP § 2272.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not issue a failure-to-respond notice for inadvertent omissions; use PTOL-467. Time continues to run; first post-final response gets one-month extension per MPEP §2265.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for entry of amendments after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments after final rejection are approved for entry only if they place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate or are in better form for appeal; otherwise they are not approved for entry. An amendment after final rejection should be denied entry if some point necessary for a complete response under 37 CFR 1.113 was omitted, even if omitted through oversight or inadvertence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission after final office action does not place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate, the response period continues to run until a proper response under 37 CFR 1.113 is filed. Same principle applies to submissions after appeal (e.g., 37 CFR 41.33) regarding appeal briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner authority to enter responses and withdraw final actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may enter the response, withdraw the final Office action, and issue a new Office action (which may be final) or an action closing prosecution under Ex parte Quayle, within the examiner's discretion. The examiner should recognize that substantial patent rights may be at issue and that the patent owner lacks the right to refile to continue prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When time has expired and an amendment would put the case in condition for certificate issuance except for an omission through oversight, the examiner should consider entering the response, withdrawing the final, and issuing an appropriate further action, mindful of the patent owner's inability to refile or request continued examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of common defective (informal) submission defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions can be 'informal' (defective). Examples of defects include: (A) paper filed does not include proof of service; (B) paper filed is unsigned; (C) paper signed by a person not of record; (D) amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); (E) amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and/or (c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTOL-475 to notify of defects prior to final rejection; check appropriate boxes and fill blanks, or attach an explanatory sheet when additional clarification is needed. Use 'other' box for defects not listed (e.g., erasable paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timing for notice of defective paper (PTOL-475)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission made prior to final rejection is defective, form PTOL-475 is used to provide notification. A time period of one month or thirty days, whichever is longer, from the mailing date of PTOL-475 will be set for correction. Extension of time to correct may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If defect not corrected within the period, submission will not be entered; failure may lead to termination of the reexamination under 37 CFR 1.550(d). After final rejection, do not use PTOL-475; use PTOL-467 advisory Office action instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirement for papers in third-party requested reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a third-party request for ex parte reexamination, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third-party requester must be served on the other party in the manner provided by § 1.248. Documents must reflect service or they may be refused consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a certificate of service to the paper specifying name, address, and method of service. A copy of the certificate must be attached to the served copy. Papers filed without proof of service may be denied consideration; reexamination clerk should call the submitter to confirm service and, if confirmed, enter the submission with an annotation 'Service confirmed by [name] on [date]'. If no service, the submission is placed in the file but normally not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy when proof of service missing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper requiring proof of service is filed without it, the reexamination clerk should contact the submitting party to determine if omission was inadvertent. If service was made, submit supplemental paper indicating manner and date of service and annotate file. If service was not made or party cannot be contacted after effort, mail PTOL-475 giving one month/30 days to supply certificate of service; if not timely made, submission may be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.15 (Lack of Service) as notice. If submission not considered because of service defect, add to IFW history as unentered paper with 'N/E' notation and annotate submission with 'no service'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to serve required papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to serve submissions has consequences: (A) For a patent owner statement or third party reply, the submission may be refused consideration and will not be addressed in the proceeding except to inform parties of lack of consideration; (B) For a patent owner response to an Office action, the response may be refused consideration and the prosecution of the proceeding may be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d), unless the patent owner has otherwise completely responded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely and proper service to avoid refusal of consideration or termination under 1.550(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition options for inappropriate or untimely papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate papers filed during reexamination will either be returned to sender or forwarded to one of three files: Reexamination File (paper or IFW), Patent File (paper or IFW), or Storage File (paper). Any papers returned from the CRU or TC must be accompanied by a letter indicating signature and approval of the CRU or TC Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an improper paper has been scanned into IFW before discovery of the inappropriate nature, it cannot be physically returned; instead expunge it by marking the paper as 'non-public' and 'closed' so it does not appear in the active IFW record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of inappropriate/returned papers by filer type
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific categories warranting return or non-consideration include: Filed by Owner — premature response prior to order to reexamine (§1.530(a), §1.540) will be returned; Paper submitted on behalf of a third party will be returned; Filed by Requester — no owner statement means requester replies are inappropriate and returned (§1.535); late response by requester (more than 2 months after service of owner’s statement) will be returned; additional responses by requester beyond the permitted reply will be returned. Third-party submissions that do not raise appropriate issues under 37 CFR 1.501 or consist solely of court decisions or litigation papers will be returned or destroyed if unidentified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return or refuse consideration based on the applicable CFR sections and the statutory limits on participation in reexamination. Petitions under 1.182/1.183 change routing to Patent Legal Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of defective papers to be placed in the Storage File
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers to be located in the Storage File include: For Owner — unsigned papers or papers signed by fewer than all owners (no attorney of record), papers lacking required proof of service, untimely papers filed after the response period; For Requester — unsigned papers, papers lacking required proof of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such papers will not be considered but are kept in storage separately from active files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of third-party citations timing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions by third parties consisting solely of prior art patents or publications filed after the date of the order to reexamine are not entered into the patent file but are delayed until the reexamination proceedings have been concluded. Proper timely filed citations (filed prior to the order) are placed in the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure third-party citations are filed before the order to be entered during reexamination; late citations are held until conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival/late paper petition fee and statutory basis
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 41 provides for revival fees; on filing each petition for revival of unintentionally abandoned application or unintentionally delayed response by the patent owner in any reexamination proceeding, a revival fee (e.g., $1,500) is charged unless filed under sections 133 or 151 (fee $500). 37 CFR 1.137 governs revival of abandoned application, terminated or limited reexamination prosecution, or lapsed patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition fees vary by statutory basis; check current §1.17 and U.S.C. provisions for correct fee amounts and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for petition based on unavoidable delay (37 CFR 1.137(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantable petition for unavoidable delay must be accompanied by: (1) The reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice (unless previously filed); (2) The petition fee set forth in §1.17(l); (3) A showing satisfactory to the Director that the entire delay was unavoidable with details and evidence; and (4) Any required terminal disclaimer and fee under §1.20(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must provide detailed circumstances and evidence supporting unavoidable delay; decisions on such petitions are made by the Office of Patent Legal Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for petition based on unintentional delay (37 CFR 1.137(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantable petition for unintentional delay must be accompanied by: (1) The reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice (unless previously filed); (2) The petition fee set forth in §1.17(m); (3) A verified statement that the entire delay was unintentional (Director may request more information); and (4) Any required terminal disclaimer and fee under §1.20(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unintentional-delay petitions require a verified statement and fee; were made applicable to reexamination by statute and implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration timing and process for denied revival petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for reconsideration or review of decisions refusing to revive under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) must be filed within two months of the decision refusing to revive (or within the time set in the decision) to be timely, and may be extended only under specified provisions (e.g., §1.136, §1.550(c), or §1.956 depending on context). Renewed petitions for reconsideration must be filed within one month of the mail date of the decision when referred to reconsideration in the MPEP text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific extension rules applicable to the type of reexamination (ex parte v inter partes) and include cover letter entitling the renewed petition under the appropriate 1.137 subsection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of ex parte reexamination prosecution for failure to timely respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.550(d), prosecution of an ex parte reexamination proceeding is terminated if the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action or any written statement of an interview required under 37 CFR 1.560(b). A terminated prosecution can be revived under 37 CFR 1.137(a) (unavoidable) or (b) (unintentional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notably, failure to timely file a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or a reply under 37 CFR 1.535 generally will not support revival under 1.137 because those failures do not ordinarily constitute 'termination' of the reexamination prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical processing and entry of compliant amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination clerk handles most initial clerical processing. CRU SPE or TC QAS provides oversight. Amendments complying with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) will be entered for purposes of reexamination in the reexamination file. New matter claim amendments must be canceled; new matter drawings ordinarily are not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For merged reissue-reexamination proceedings see MPEP §2283 and §2285. Where an amendment enlarges claim scope, it may be entered but appropriate claims will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and process for making a final action in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a final action, a clear issue should be developed; the examiner will provide information/references twice to define the Office position (decision ordering reexamination and first Office action). The second Office action will generally be made final, analogous to MPEP §706.07(a). In making the final rejection, all outstanding grounds should be carefully reviewed and reiterated so the patent owner may readily judge advisability of appeal; if a previous OA contains a complete statement of a ground, the final may refer to it and include rebuttal to owner arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that reexamination can lead to cancellation; patent owner cannot renew/continue prosecution by refiling; encourage complete early presentation of evidence under 37 CFR 1.131/1.132 to avoid problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference requirement before final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner determines the proceeding is ready for final rejection, the examiner formulates a draft preliminary decision specifying which claims to reject/allow and reasons, informs the CRU SPE or TC QAS, who convenes a panel review conference. Conference members review claim patentability pursuant to MPEP §2271.01. If the conference confirms the preliminary decision, the final rejection is issued and signed by the examiner with two conferees initialing; if not confirmed, the examiner reevaluates and issues an appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel review provides quality control and confirmation prior to issuing a final rejection in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of art submitted by patent owner during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Where art is submitted in a prior art citation under 37 CFR 1.501 and/or 1.555 (IDS construed as prior art citation) and the submission is not accompanied by a statement similar to 37 CFR 1.97(e), the examiner may use the art and make the next Office action final whether or not the claims have been amended, provided no other new ground of rejection is introduced by the examiner based on new art not cited in the prior art citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner supplies art without required statement, the examiner has discretion to treat it as material and proceed to final action absent introduction of new grounds based on other new art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for final action notices (22.09 and 22.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.09: 'THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.' Sets a shortened statutory period for response (normally two months) and explains that extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 do not apply; extensions per 37 CFR 1.550(c) may be requested for sufficient cause and require petition fee. Filing a timely first response to the final rejection is construed as requesting an additional one-month extension; statutory period not later than six months. Form paragraph 22.10: similar, used where patent owner's amendment necessitated the new grounds of rejection; includes brackets for insertion of filing/response dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these form paragraphs only in reexamination proceedings. Insert appropriate periods (normally two months) and follow instructions for court-sanctioned or stayed litigation situations (one month). Final Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.
